---
title: "Architecture"
---

## Verdict

Cellerator should be designed as a compiler and runtime for biological sparse programs.

It should not be centered on:

- a matrix class;
- Blocked-ELL;
- a file format;
- SpMM;
- Torch;
- CellShard;
- one GPU generation.

Matrices and sparse formats remain important mathematical and physical views. They are not the universal semantic object.

## Architectural layers

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    A[Biological domains and typed relations]
    B[Immutable structures and mutable value planes]
    C[CellPack / CP-BP semantic geometry compiler]
    D[Projection catalog]
    E[Core planner and autotuner]
    F[Prepared operations and execution programs]
    G[Native, vendor, sequence-fused, and distributed kernels]
    H[Expression, regulatory, latent, and downstream state]

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
```

### Biological ABI

The shared ABI defines:

- domains;
- axis identity;
- order identity;
- geometry identity;
- partition identity;
- relation identity;
- structure epoch;
- value generation;
- dense, bit-plane, event, segment, and sparse-relation operand views;
- stream and device binding contracts.

This ABI must remain small enough for Baseplane and adapters to consume without importing the full core runtime.

### Structure and value layer

A logical relation separates topology from numbers.

```cpp
struct relation_structure {
    structure_id identity;
    std::uint64_t structure_epoch;

    domain_id source_domain;
    domain_id destination_domain;

    order_id source_order;
    order_id destination_order;

    projection_catalog projections;
};

struct value_plane {
    const relation_structure* structure;

    void* values;
    dtype storage_type;
    dtype logical_type;

    quantization_descriptor quantization;
    std::uint64_t value_generation;
};
```

Examples:

- fixed enhancer-to-gene topology with changing accessibility or regulatory weights;
- fixed GRN topology shared across cells;
- fixed sparse neural topology with changing learned values;
- fixed sequence-derived motif relation reused across state evaluations;
- one structure with fp16, bf16, int8, and fp32 value planes.

### CellPack and CP-BP compiler

The compiler observes biological regularity and produces semantic execution geometry.

It owns:

- sampling;
- support extraction;
- candidate generation;
- exact or calibrated cost;
- row and feature ordering;
- module and partition construction;
- geometry validation;
- scheduling statistics;
- execution-image construction.

It does not own canonical storage, network transport, or final kernel selection.

### Projection catalog

A semantic structure may have several physical projections:

```text
row-masked warp tiles
feature-major masked tiles
CTA macro-tiles
dense MMA fragments
CSR
SELL-C-sigma
BSR
Blocked-ELL
transpose or backward views
quantized value layouts
```

A projection is selected for an operation, device, precision, and reuse regime.

### Core planner and autotuner

The core planner:

1. validates semantics and identities;
2. enumerates legal projections and kernels;
3. rejects incompatible candidates;
4. estimates complete cost;
5. benchmarks a bounded shortlist where necessary;
6. caches measured results;
7. chooses graph-wide orders and conversions;
8. produces reusable prepared operations or programs.

### Prepared execution

A prepared operation binds long-lived state:

- structure;
- projection;
- kernel;
- backend descriptors;
- persistent preprocessing;
- workspace requirements;
- graph-capture metadata.

A launch binding supplies short-lived state:

- current value plane;
- dense input;
- output;
- bias;
- scalar coefficients;
- stream;
- transient workspace.

Changing a pointer or stream must not require structure planning again.

### Execution program

Several prepared operations may be composed into a graph with:

- execution-order propagation;
- fused producer-consumer boundaries;
- explicit order transformations;
- communication steps;
- graph replay;
- persistent work queues.

The graph optimizer chooses a globally useful order rather than the fastest isolated kernel when local selection would create costly permutations.

## Canonical order

Canonical order is important for:

- persistence;
- interoperability;
- user-facing output;
- exact identity;
- debugging;
- reference validation.

It is not the normal internal order.

An internal operation should return canonical order only when:

- an external consumer requires it;
- the next operation is demonstrably faster after canonicalization;
- canonical order is itself the selected execution order;
- correctness or communication requires it.

Every other canonicalization is a candidate performance defect.

## Semantic geometry

Semantic geometry is relatively stable organization:

- which entities are grouped;
- how entities are ordered;
- how groups nest;
- which partitions own them;
- which cross-group edges exist;
- how canonical identity is recovered.

It may be workload- and deployment-aware. It is not required to be device-neutral.

Two byte layouts with the same order and groups are physical projections of one geometry. Two different feature permutations or GPU partitions are different geometries.

## Physical projections

A physical projection is a concrete ingestion contract for a kernel.

It specifies:

- memory sections;
- index widths;
- mask encoding;
- value order;
- alignment;
- tile shape;
- orientation;
- padding;
- local scheduling summaries;
- forward or transpose direction;
- precision and quantization.

Physical projections are disposable and replaceable. Semantic identities survive their replacement.

## Hierarchy

Biological hierarchy should be represented as overlapping relations and nested execution partitions, not as duplicated value trees.

Possible views include:

```text
cell
  → regulatory program
      → module
          → regulatory element group
              → gene
                  → transcript
```

Real biology is not a strict tree. Modules, pathways, enhancers, and genes overlap. Several hierarchy indices may refer to one underlying value plane.

Hierarchy remains in the runtime image only when it enables:

- module skipping;
- local reductions;
- cache reuse;
- shared-memory staging;
- kernel specialization;
- quantization;
- prefetching;
- communication partitioning;
- level-of-detail execution.

Otherwise it stays compiler or interpretation metadata.

## Execution image

The successful CPK1 principle should evolve into a sectioned execution image.

```text
ExecutionImageHeader
Domain table
Order and partition table
Relation and structure table
Projection directory
Optional physical projection sections
Forward and transpose value maps
Hierarchy and boundary-edge indices
Compact scheduling summaries
```

The image uses:

- explicit versions;
- relative offsets;
- lengths and capacities;
- stable identities;
- alignment;
- independent section validation.

CellShard may wrap and transport the image as opaque bytes. Cellerator owns its semantics and rebinding.

## Core ownership

### Cellerator

Owns:

- biological execution semantics;
- shared ABI;
- structure and values;
- geometry and projections;
- planner and kernels;
- numerical state;
- graph and order optimization.

### Baseplane

Owns sequence-specialized representations and primitives within the Cellerator umbrella.

### CellShard

Owns persistence, delivery, staging, generation, and distributed data movement.

### CelleraTorch

Owns framework adaptation.

## Architecture-specific execution

Stable contracts must support several NVIDIA generations.

Portable across generations:

- biological identities;
- relation semantics;
- structure and value lifetime;
- semantic geometry;
- projection kinds;
- planner keys;
- execution-image sections.

Generation-specific:

- tile dimensions;
- shared-memory staging;
- asynchronous copies;
- MMA shape;
- warp specialization;
- persistent CTA policy;
- cache operators;
- launch parameters.

Runtime dispatch selects the implementation.

## Design constraints

A new core design is acceptable only when:

- identities remain exact;
- structure and values remain separable;
- conversion cost is visible;
- multiple projections remain possible;
- the hot path is allocation-free;
- graph capture is not accidentally prohibited;
- training and transpose needs are considered;
- Baseplane can participate without a foreign tensor boundary;
- CellShard remains storage and transport only;
- performance can be falsified by a stronger baseline.

## Non-goals

The architecture does not require:

- one universal kernel;
- one universal format;
- one universal semantic geometry;
- a large dynamic C++ object hierarchy;
- a general compiler frontend before the core ABI works;
- biological labels in hot kernels;
- Tensor Cores in every path;
- custom kernels when vendor libraries are faster.

A somewhat untidy hybrid is preferable to a beautiful system that moves more bytes.
